edges.mechanism: Pyridoxine/pyridoxamine 5'-phosphate oxidase (PNPO) that forms PLP is FMN-dependent; plasma PLP falls stepwise with worsening riboflavin status independent of B6 intake, especially in older adults and MTHFR 677TT carriers.
edges.evidence: Large cross-sectional cohorts (n>5000 combined) plus mechanistic review; no RCT of co-supplementation on clinical outcomes

edges.mechanism: Riboflavin (FAD) is the MTHFR cofactor upstream of 5-MTHF formation; in MTHFR 677TT, riboflavin lowers homocysteine and 5-MTHF bypasses the enzyme. Complementary routes for one-carbon support; folate, not riboflavin, lowered homocysteine in elderly with low riboflavin status.
edges.evidence: Genotype-stratified RCTs of riboflavin; RCT of L-methylfolate vs folinic acid; low certainty for added benefit of combining

edges.mechanism: Methionine synthase reductase requires FMN and FAD to regenerate methylcobalamin for B12-dependent methionine synthase.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic (biochemistry review); no clinical interaction trial

edges.mechanism: Riboflavin is a standard B-complex/multivitamin component; stacking adds to total dose and intensifies yellow urine and urinary flavin excretion (B1+B2 100 mg each raised urinary B2 ~20-fold).
edges.evidence: Reference monograph; small RCT measuring urinary B2

edges.mechanism: Riboflavin cofactors are needed for iron mobilisation from ferritin for erythropoiesis; correcting low riboflavin status improves hemoglobin and the response of iron-deficiency anemia to iron. No study used heme iron specifically.
edges.evidence: RCT in UK women (RIBOFEM); RCT in anemic pregnant women with iron-folate; review

edges.mechanism: Complementary migraine preventives (mitochondrial energy vs neuronal excitability); both recommended individually by CHS and Level B by AAN/AHS. Fixed riboflavin+magnesium+Q10 combination reduced migraine burden but not migraine days; riboflavin 400 mg+Mg+feverfew did not beat riboflavin 25 mg.
edges.evidence: Guidelines; 2 combination RCTs; MAs of single agents; low certainty for additive effect

edges.mechanism: Both target mitochondrial energy metabolism in migraine; CoQ10 was strongly recommended by CHS and Level C by AAN/AHS. Combination with riboflavin and magnesium reduced migraine intensity and HIT-6.
edges.evidence: Guidelines, CoQ10 RCT and MAs, network MA 2026, combination RCT; low certainty for additive effect

edges.mechanism: Imipramine and amitriptyline (structural riboflavin analogues) inhibit flavokinase and riboflavin-to-FAD conversion in rat tissues; possible reduced riboflavin status with long-term use.
edges.evidence: Animal/in vitro data; no human outcome data

edges.mechanism: Chlorpromazine inhibits flavokinase, doubles urinary riboflavin loss and accelerates tissue FAD depletion in riboflavin-deficient rats; inhibits renal tubular riboflavin transport.
edges.evidence: Animal and isolated tubule studies; no human outcome data

edges.mechanism: Riboflavin is secreted by renal organic-anion transport; probenecid inhibits tubular riboflavin secretion (rabbit tubules) and its effect on renal riboflavin clearance was studied in humans.
edges.evidence: Human PK study (1970) and in vitro tubule perfusion; clinical significance unknown

edges.mechanism: Long-term use may increase hepatic destruction of riboflavin, raising deficiency risk.
edges.evidence: Reference monograph statement; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Adriamycin (doxorubicin) and the antimalarial quinacrine inhibit conversion of riboflavin to FMN/FAD; some anticancer and antimicrobial drugs increase renal riboflavin excretion.
edges.evidence: Reference monograph and review; mechanistic

edges.mechanism: In MTHFR 677TT patients already on antihypertensives, riboflavin 1.6 mg/d lowered SBP further (5.6 mmHg vs placebo; 6-13 mmHg across trials).
edges.evidence: Genotype-targeted RCTs; Cochrane review across genotypes very uncertain

edges.mechanism: FAD-dependent MTHFR variant; riboflavin lowers homocysteine (~22%) and blood pressure only in TT homozygotes; TT with deficient riboflavin status has OR 3.0 for hypertension.
edges.evidence: Genotype-stratified RCTs, 4-y follow-up, population cohort (JINGO), case-control; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Defective RFVT2/RFVT3 transport causes flavin deficiency with motor/cranial neuronopathy and deafness; high-dose riboflavin is lifesaving and should be started empirically; outcome depends on time to treatment.
edges.evidence: Case series and SR (90.4% responsive, n=94); natural-history review

edges.mechanism: ETF:QO (ETFDH) and FAD synthase (FLAD1) defects are partly corrected by pharmacological riboflavin restoring flavoprotein activity.
edges.evidence: Case series; SR of IMDs (MADD type 3 93.1% responsive, n=536; type 1 not responsive)

edges.mechanism: 400 mg/d for >=3 months reduces attack frequency (WMD -1.39/month); AAN/AHS Level B, CHS strong recommendation; pediatric evidence inconsistent.
edges.evidence: Multiple SR/MAs of RCTs, guidelines; moderate certainty in adults

edges.mechanism: Riboflavin is a urinary fluorophore; 200-400 mg doses raised background fluorescence causing MX BKG errors on Abbott TDx drugs-of-abuse assays within hours, clearing ~60 h after stopping; no false negatives seen.
edges.evidence: Forensic toxicology case study (2 subjects)

edges.mechanism: Vitamin B2 was the only tested substance altering the urine fluorescence spectrum; high doses produce bright-yellow urine (flavinuria).
edges.evidence: Experimental study of vitamins/foods; reference monographs

edges.with: EGRAC riboflavin status assay in G6PD deficiency
edges.mechanism: EGRAC cannot be used to assess riboflavin status in glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency; results are also sensitive to methodological variation.
edges.evidence: ODS fact sheet; methodological study

edges.mechanism: Riboflavin is photolabile; prolonged phototherapy can deplete riboflavin and accentuate the postnatal decline of PLP.
edges.evidence: Observational neonatal study; ODS
